prompt: You want "add x to every element of `a[l..r]`" and "what is `a[i]`?" using a single Fenwick tree. Which approach works in O(log n) per operation?

options.text: Store differences: `add(l, x)` and `add(r + 1, -x)`; then `a[i]` is `prefix(i)`
options.explanation: Correct. The tree holds neighbouring differences; summing their prefix reconstructs the corresponding element. A range add changes only two differences.

options.text: Call `add(k, x)` for every k from l to r
options.explanation: That is one update per element in the range, O(n log n) for a range covering most of the n elements.
This raises every element from l onwards, including those after r.

options.text: Store the array normally and answer `a[i]` with `range_sum(i, i)`
options.explanation: Point queries work, but range updates are still O(n log n) with this layout, where n is the array length.

workedExample: Store the differences between neighbours. Adding at the left boundary starts an increase in every later reconstructed value; adding the opposite amount just after the right boundary cancels it for later positions. Internal differences remain unchanged because both neighbours increased together. A prefix of differences reconstructs one value. These are a fixed number of O(log n) Fenwick calls for n elements.
